analysis.title: Real Estate in a 5% World
key_insights: The ten-year Treasury rose above 5% in September 2026, a level reached only once since 2007 (briefly in October 2023). Real estate yields now sit about 0.6 points above the ten-year, roughly a fifth of the long-run average spread.

The all-sector NCREIF transaction cap rate is about 90 basis points below Baa-rated corporate bond yields. Historically real estate yielded slightly less than Baa bonds only rarely. Apollo says the Treasury is a real benchmark again.

Apollo's view is that real estate offers a selective set of opportunities. It sees value where current income or income growth pays for the excess risk over the ten-year, and expects more to emerge as conditions change.

Investors are paid for the extra risk today in real estate lending (conventional commercial through data centers), seniors housing, certain retail, and certain apartment and warehouse markets with little new supply.

Senior commercial property loans carry fixed rates of roughly 6.5% to 7.5%. Pre-leased data center campuses price lower, at about 6.25%. Core apartments and warehouses yield about 4.1% to 4.3% on appraised values and about 5% on recent sales.
A fixed-rate loan coupon does not grow, while an owner's income can. Operations and income growth are therefore where equity earns its place, and the opportunity set cannot depend on lower rates.
Manufactured housing example: site rental income at the largest listed owners rose about 6% in the year to 2Q 2026. With little return paid up front, the sector is more exposed to a higher Treasury.

Since the 2Q 2022 value peak, the ten-year rose about 3.5 points and cap rates about 1.2 points. NCREIF same-property NOI is up about 15% while appraised values are down about 19%. Apollo attributes the decline to rates, not weaker buildings.

Repricing has shown up in actual sales but not yet in appraisals. Properties sold over the past ten quarters changed hands at yields about 1 point above appraised values, twice the normal gap. Appraised values have been flat for six quarters. Apollo suggests reading reported values alongside sale prices.

Supply is back within normal range. Apartments under construction are down by more than half from the 2023 peak, starts are nearly two-thirds below 2022, and apartment vacancy peaked at 7.0% at end-2025 and has begun to fall.
Seniors housing construction is under a third of its pre-pandemic pace, with occupancy above 2019 levels and rents up near 5% over the past year.
Warehouses are the exception: construction is above its post-2008 average, vacancy is rising, and leasing is at a fifteen-year low. Only select markets pay for the risk.

Apollo views apartments market by market: attractive now in supply-constrained coastal and mid-sized markets, a recovery opportunity in overbuilt Sunbelt markets once pipelines are absorbed, and wait where supply is low but vacancy is high.

Demand support: owning a median-priced home costs about $775 a month more than renting, first-time buyers are 21% of purchases (lowest on record), the 65+ population is 64.6 million (+16% since 2020), and AI spending has pushed major-market data center vacancy to 1.4% with 80% of a record pipeline pre-leased.
Net international migration fell by more than half from its 2024 peak, which weighs on apartment demand.
Apollo is patient on core apartments and warehouses at current prices. Cap rates of 4% to 5% against a 5% Treasury and 6.5% to 7.5% loan rates mean borrowing lowers returns.

Catalyst: $875 billion of commercial property loans mature in 2026 and $652 billion in 2027 (about 30% of all such debt). Roughly a fifth of 2025 maturities were extended rather than repaid. The 2026 maturity total was revised up more than 30% in a year.

Banks eased commercial real estate lending standards in all three loan categories in 3Q 2026 for the first time since 2022, which Apollo sees as a precondition for refinancings to clear and price discovery to begin.
Apollo says returns from here come from income, income growth and purchase price, not falling rates or markups. Half of the last cycle's return came from rising values.
Investors in real estate debt are paid while they wait. Investors holding capital for core property may find better entry points as loans come due over the next two years.

sector_views.rationale: Senior loans pay 6.5% to 7.5%, well above the 5% Treasury. Pre-leased data center loans price near 6.25%.
Construction is below a third of pre-pandemic pace, occupancy is 88.9% against 85.9% in 4Q 2019, and rents are up about 4.9% over the past year.
Rents are already rising and supply is constrained, so income growth can make up the thin yield spread.
A recovery opportunity at reset prices once pipelines of 3% to 7% of stock are absorbed. Apollo wants two straight quarters of rent growth above core inflation.
Vacancy is 8% to 14%, leasing is at a fifteen-year low, and supply has outrun demand. Only select markets pay for the risk.

sector_views.sector: Core apartments and warehouses at current prices
sector_views.rationale: Cap rates of 4% to 5% against a 5% Treasury and 6.5% to 7.5% loan rates mean borrowing lowers returns.
Certain retail trades at yields above the Treasury, with sale cap rates of 5.9% versus 5.0% for the ten-year.
Sells at yields well above the Treasury (7.1% transaction cap rate), but Apollo notes fundamentals are structurally impaired.

earnings_insights: Equity LifeStyle Properties, quarter ended June 30, 2026 vs the same quarter of 2025: core portfolio manufactured housing base rental income +5.8% (average monthly base rent per site $956 vs $904). Reported figure.
Sun Communities, quarter ended June 30, 2026 vs the same quarter of 2025: same-property manufactured housing revenue +6.2% and net operating income +8.8%. Reported figure.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Highest since 2007 on a closing basis, last 5% intraday in October 2023. Apollo says the move has been almost entirely real yields: 83 bp YTD, of which 72 bp is the ten-year TIPS yield (1.90% to 2.62%) and 13 bp breakeven inflation.
1.48 points above the ten-year, against a 2001-2019 average spread of 2.66 points.

macro_indicators.indicator: ICE BofA US Corporate Index option-adjusted spread
macro_indicators.interpretation: Compared with a 2001-2019 average of 1.58 points, so investment-grade spreads are narrow too.
Base for senior loan pricing, plus spreads of roughly 175 to 275 bp gives 6.5% to 7.5% fixed coupons.
Apollo cites it as the bar rent growth needs to exceed for core apartments to re-rate.

macro_indicators.indicator: NCREIF NPI all-property transaction cap rate
macro_indicators.interpretation: About 0.6 points above the ten-year against a 2001-2019 average spread of 2.96 points, in the bottom 5% of quarterly readings since 2001.

macro_indicators.indicator: Net tightening of CRE lending standards (Fed SLOOS)
macro_indicators.reading: -11.3 nonfarm nonresidential, -5.7 multifamily, -3.7 construction and land
macro_indicators.interpretation: First net easing in all three categories since 2022, after 64% to 74% net tightening peaks in 2023.

risk_factors: Higher Treasury yields further compress real estate's spread, especially for low-yield, growth-dependent sectors such as manufactured housing and core apartments.
Appraised values have not caught up with transaction prices, so reported values may overstate current worth.
Warehouse vacancy is rising and leasing is at a fifteen-year low.
Office fundamentals are structurally impaired despite high yields.
Lower immigration, with net international migration down by more than half from its 2024 peak, weakens apartment demand.
Sunbelt apartment supply is still 3% to 7% of existing stock, with national vacancy at 6.7% and rent growth under 1%.
Loan extensions have delayed price discovery. A fifth of 2025 maturities were extended.
charts_described: Exhibit 1: With the ten-year at 5.00%, apartment appraisal cap rate 4.3% (-0.7 vs Treasury), industrial 4.1% (-0.9), retail 5.3% (+0.3), office 5.7% (+0.7). Recent-sale cap rates are apartments 5.0% (+0.0), industrial 4.9% (-0.1), retail 5.9% (+0.9), office 7.1% (+2.1). Baa yields are +1.5 and senior loans +2.0 versus the Treasury.
Exhibit 2 Panel A: Real estate yield over the ten-year averaged 3.0 points in 2001-2019 against 2.7 for Baa, and at 9/15/2026 is +0.6 for real estate and +1.5 for Baa.
Exhibit 2 Panel B: Since 2Q 2022 property values (appraised) are down 19% and property income (same properties) up 15%, with the transaction income yield at 5.6% and the appraisal yield at 4.6%.

Exhibit 3: Space under construction as a share of existing stock versus 2008-2026 normal range. Apartments are 0.3 standard deviations below average, warehouses 0.6 above, retail 0.5 below, office 1.7 below, seniors housing 1.2 below.

tension_points.bull_case: Occupancy in core apartments, warehouses and retail is above its 30-year average, NOI is up about 15%, and supply has returned to normal. Rent growth returning above inflation would let income growth close the yield gap.
tension_points.bear_case: Cap rates of 4% to 5% sit against a 5% Treasury and 6.5% to 7.5% loan rates, so borrowing lowers returns. Sale prices run about 1 point of yield above appraisals, so values may still have to fall.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Apollo would turn constructive if loan rates fell below property income yields, or if the gap between sale and appraised yields narrowed from about 1 point toward its 0.5 point norm. It also wants two straight quarters of rent growth above core inflation, with falling vacancy, in the Sunbelt apartment markets.

tension_points.bull_case: Refinancing at today's rates prompts sales and recapitalizations that move appraisals toward sale prices and widen the buyer's opportunity. Banks are easing standards.
tension_points.bear_case: Loan extensions have delayed price discovery. About a fifth of 2025 maturities were extended, and the 2026 maturity total was revised up more than 30% in a year.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Watch the MBA maturity schedule, loans in special servicing, and the gap between sale and appraised prices.

theme_stances.key_argument: With the ten-year at 5%, real estate yields are only about 0.6 points above Treasuries, so investors are paid for risk only in selective areas.
theme_stances.evidence: The question for each type of real estate is simple: is the investor paid for the risk?

theme_stances.key_argument: Lenders earn 6.5% to 7.5% fixed while core owners earn 4% to 5%, and real estate debt investors are paid while they wait for entry points.
theme_stances.evidence: Investors in real estate debt are paid while they wait.

theme_stances.key_argument: $1.5 trillion of property loans due in 2026-27 may force sales and recapitalizations that widen buyer opportunities.
theme_stances.evidence: We believe the opportunity can widen as $1.5 trillion of property loans come due
